es.term: Tos por inhibidores de la ECA
es.summary: La tos seca persistente es un efecto adverso frecuente de los inhibidores de la ECA, causada por acumulación de bradiquinina en las vías respiratorias.
key_points: Aparece en 5-20% de los pacientes y suele ser seca y no productiva.
Mecanismo: inhibición de la degradación de bradiquinina y sustancia P.
Puede provocar discontinuación del tratamiento y mala adherencia.
Si la tos es severa o se acompaña de angioedema, se debe considerar cambiar a un ARA II.
La tos suele mejorar al 4‑6 semanas o al suspender el fármaco.

mechanism: Los IECA inhiben la enzima que degrada bradiquinina.
El aumento de bradiquinina irrita los receptores C en la mucosa bronquial.
La irritación genera tos seca sin producción de esputo.
adverse_effects: Angioedema de labios, lengua o vías respiratorias (grave).
Hiperkalemia (grave, especialmente con diuréticos ahorradores de K).
interactions: AINEs pueden aumentar riesgo de insuficiencia renal y potenciar hiperpotasemia.
Diuréticos ahorradores de potasio aumentan riesgo de hiperkalemia.
Suplementos de potasio o sustitutos de sal pueden agravar la hiperkalemia.
nursing_care: Evaluar frecuencia, intensidad y patrón de la tos antes y después de iniciar IECA.
Auscultar pulmones para descartar otras causas (neumonía, EPOC).
Retener el IECA y notificar al médico si la tos es severa o hay angioedema.
Documentar la respuesta del paciente al cambio de medicación.
patient_teaching: Informar que la tos es un efecto esperado y suele ser temporal.
Indicar que debe reportar tos que interfiere con el sueño o habla de hinchazón facial.
Recomendar hidratación adecuada y evitar irritantes (tabaco, polvo).
Explicar que cambiar a un bloqueador del receptor de angiotensina (ARA II) puede eliminar la tos.

related_to: uso de inhibidores de la ECA
outcomes: Control de la tos: reducción a <2 episodios/día en 48 h
Calidad del sueño: dormir ≥6 horas nocturnas en 3 días

interventions.action: Evaluar la intensidad y frecuencia de la tos usando escala de 0‑10.
interventions.rationale: Permite cuantificar el problema y valorar la necesidad de intervención.

interventions.action: Auscultar los pulmones y observar signos de angioedema.
interventions.rationale: Descarta complicaciones graves que requieran atención inmediata.

interventions.action: Retener el IECA y notificar al médico si la tos es severa o hay edema facial.
interventions.rationale: Previene progresión a angioedema y permite considerar cambio a ARA II.

interventions.action: Educar al paciente sobre la posible sustitución por ARB y la importancia de la adherencia.
interventions.rationale: Facilita la continuidad del tratamiento antihipertensivo.

interventions.action: Fomentar hidratación y evitar irritantes ambientales.
interventions.rationale: Reduce la irritación de la mucosa y alivia la tos.

en.summary: Persistent dry cough is a common adverse effect of ACE inhibitors, caused by accumulation of bradykinin in the airways.
key_points: Occurs in 5-20% of patients and is usually dry and nonproductive.
Mechanism: inhibition of bradykinin and substance P degradation.
Can lead to discontinuation of therapy and poor adherence.
If cough is severe or accompanied by angioedema, consider switching to an ARB.
Cough usually improves within 4‑6 weeks or after stopping the drug.

mechanism: ACEIs inhibit the enzyme that degrades bradykinin.
Increased bradykinin irritates C receptors in bronchial mucosa.
Irritation produces dry cough without sputum production.
adverse_effects: Angioedema of lips, tongue, or airways (severe).
interactions: NSAIDs can increase risk of renal failure and potentiate hyperkalemia.
Potassium‑sparing diuretics increase risk of hyperkalemia.
Potassium supplements or salt substitutes can worsen hyperkalemia.
nursing_care: Assess frequency, intensity, and pattern of cough before and after starting ACEI.
Listen to lungs to rule out other causes (pneumonia, COPD).
Hold the ACEI and notify the provider if cough is severe or angioedema occurs.
Document patient response to medication change.
patient_teaching: Inform that cough is an expected and usually temporary effect.
Advise reporting cough that interferes with sleep or speech of facial swelling.
Recommend adequate hydration and avoidance of irritants (tobacco, dust).
Explain that switching to an angiotensin receptor blocker (ARB) may eliminate the cough.

evidenced_by: fatigue due to lack of rest
outcomes: Control of cough: reduction to <2 episodes/day within 48 h
Sleep quality: sleep ≥6 hours nightly for 3 days

interventions.action: Assess cough intensity and frequency using a 0‑10 scale.
interventions.rationale: Allows quantification of the problem and assessment of need for intervention.

interventions.action: Listen to lungs and observe for signs of angioedema.
interventions.rationale: Rules out serious complications requiring immediate attention.

interventions.action: Hold the ACEI and notify the provider if cough is severe or facial edema occurs.
interventions.rationale: Prevents progression to angioedema and allows consideration of ARB switch.

interventions.action: Educate patient about possible substitution with ARB and importance of adherence.
Encourage hydration and avoidance of environmental irritants.
interventions.rationale: Reduces mucosal irritation and alleviates cough.

sections.mechanism.0.quote: Inhibits the enzyme that converts angiotensin I to angiotensin II and thereby suppresses the renin-angiotensin-aldosterone system

sections.mechanism.2.quote: Clients may develop an ACE inhibitor–associated cough (a persistent, dry, itchy cough), hyperkalemia (elevated potassium level in the blood), or hypotension (Jun et al., 2021).

sections.adverse_effects.0.quote: Clients may develop an ACE inhibitor–associated cough (a persistent, dry, itchy cough), hyperkalemia (elevated potassium level in the blood), or hypotension (Jun et al., 2021).

sections.adverse_effects.1.quote: Adverse effects include angioedema, nonproductive cough, neutropenia (low neutrophils in the blood), agranulocytosis (low granulocytes in the blood), proteinuria (protein in the urine), and rash.

sections.adverse_effects.2.quote: Clients may develop an ACE inhibitor–associated cough (a persistent, dry, itchy cough), hyperkalemia (elevated potassium level in the blood), or hypotension (Jun et al., 2021).

sections.interactions.2.quote: Taking ACE inhibitors with potassium-containing salt substitutes or consuming large amounts of high potassium foods increases the risk of hyperkalemia.
